newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, but outperforming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, but outperforming.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were unchanged in early trading Friday, continuing to outperform the softer Treasury market because of a slim new issue calendar.
"It's the same story of the past three weeks," one trader said. "The light calendar and favorable technicals are keeping prices higher."

The government market lost ground after the Commerce Department said housing starts for April were up 2.6 percent to a 1.473 million unit annual rate. That was slightly higher-than-expected, as Wall Street economists had forecast starts at a 1.43 million rate.
The long bond shed 6/32, moving to 96-24/32 and pushing the yield higher to 6.88 percent.

Traders said Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee will keep a lid on activity Friday and Monday, as investors remain sidelined by conflicting views of where short-term rates are headed.
In debt futures Friday, the June municipal contract was down 2/32 to 116-8/32, while June T-bonds lost 4/32 to 110-6/32. The MOB spread widened to 194 ticks from 192 at the close Thursday.

Secondary market bids on Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up two basis points to 5.85 percent. Orange County, Fla., School Board MBIA 5-3/8s of 2022 were down one basis point t o5.70 percent.
Preliminary estimates of next week's supply total $2.4 billion.
Lehman Brothers is slated to bring a $750 million New York City GO deal on Wednesday. The offering, the week's largest, is one of 29 scheduled negotiated issues totaling $1.5 billion.
Tuesday's $285 million Nevada offering is the largest scheduled competive offering. Seventy-seven competitive issues totaling $924 million are scheduled next week.
